owner_signature_observed.meaning: a valid on-chain ECDSA signature from an AtomWallet owner is observable after an executed UserOp

high_s_counterpart_derived.meaning: adversary has derived a high-s counterpart of the valid owner signature via s' = secp256k1_order - s and v' = v XOR 1, recovering the identical signer address

bundler_distinguishes_wallet_revert.meaning: the bundler's error handling distinguishes a wallet revert from a transient failure
bundler_distinguishes_wallet_revert.checkpoint: during bundler error handling of the griefing UserOp

bundler_retry_or_blacklist_occurs.meaning: the bundler retries or blacklists the targeted AtomWallet because it did not distinguish the wallet revert from a transient failure
bundler_retry_or_blacklist_occurs.checkpoint: after bundler error handling of the griefing UserOp

assumptions: The griefing UserOp carrying the derived high-s signature is submitted to an AtomWallet and simulated by a bundler.
The bundler's error handling is the point at which a wallet revert could be misclassified as a transient failure.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the griefing UserOp was actually observed on-chain; the retry/blacklist effect is described as potential and conditional on the bundler's error handling.
Report does not specify which bundler implementation or error-handling behavior is in scope, so the distinguishing behavior is represented as a grounded Boolean rather than a numeric relation.

limitations: The retry/blacklist outcome is formalized as a Boolean occurrence because the report gives no numeric or structural definition of the bundler's error-handling decision.
Other impacts (bundler compute waste, batch transaction failure, wallet degradation) are not covered by this plan and are handled in separate claim-generation passes.
